NKE.thesis_one_line: World's largest sportswear brand, mid-turnaround and over 50% off its highs, but the latest 'beat' was mostly a one-time tariff-refund windfall.
kill_criteria: Underlying gross margin (excluding any tariff-refund benefit) fails to expand YoY in FQ2 FY2027 (quarter ending ~2026-11-30) as management explicitly guided.
Greater China segment revenue or EBIT (as reported each quarter) declines by more than 15% YoY for two more consecutive quarters (vs. -20% for FY2026 overall).
Full-year free cash flow (OCF minus capex) for FY2027 comes in below FY2026's approximately $2.18bn (the multi-year FCF decline continues into year three).
Net debt/EBITDA rises above 1.0x (from approximately net-debt-neutral today) without a specific, disclosed strategic rationale.
The pending consumer class action (Portland, OR, filed 2026-05-08) or the securities-related investigation results in a material adverse ruling, settlement, or confirmed SEC enforcement action.
key_adverse_facts: FQ4 FY2026's headline 890bps gross-margin gain and $0.72 diluted EPS were overwhelmingly a one-time, non-recurring $986M IEEPA tariff-refund benefit (~900bps of the margin gain, $0.52 of the $0.72 EPS); ex-benefit gross margin was 40.2%, essentially flat YoY.

Full-year free cash flow fell 33% YoY (FY2026 ~$2.18bn vs FY2025 ~$3.27bn) and includes ~$0.3bn of one-off tariff-recovery cash; after $715m of stock-based compensation, normalised FCF is only ~$1.17bn (DV30).

Post-cutoff (1 Oct 2026) FQ1 FY27 release: revenue $11.2bn (-4%), diluted EPS $0.48, gross margin 42.8% (+60bps); FY27 outlook revenue down high-single digits (the dossier relied on 'low single digits' from secondary sources) and adjusted EPS $1.15-1.35, with the new 'Pace' programme (~$1.0bn pre-tax charges through FY2031, ~$0.3bn in FY27) (DV30).
Greater China segment EBIT down 20% for the full fiscal year; management guides continued marketplace cleanup through FY2027 with no near-term stabilization promised.

A proposed consumer class action (filed 2026-05-08, Portland OR) alleges Nike is retaining IEEPA tariff refunds; law-firm-led securities investigations are also circling the March 2026 stock decline (investigation stage only).
data_conflicts: Q01 triage flagged Nike as 'advance' citing the stock's post-selloff dividend yield and a management claim of a coming gross-margin inflection, but did not identify that the most recent quarter's reported margin/EPS beat was overwhelmingly a one-time IEEPA tariff-refund item rather than organic improvement; this dossier corrects that framing without changing the 'advance' conclusion.
NKE.confidence_in_thesis: low-medium -- balance sheet and the one-off separation are well sourced, but SBC was omitted from the valuation, the corrected reverse DCF requires more growth than the base case, and the 1 Oct 2026 outlook (revenue down high-single digits, adjusted EPS $1.15-1.35) post-dates and weakens the thesis (DV30)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: DV30 (2026-10-08): the original reverse DCF did not deduct stock-based compensation ($715m in FY2026, 38% of the ~$1.88bn tariff-normalised FCF). On the programme basis (FCF after SBC, Ke 8.5%, terminal growth 2.5-3.0%, market cap $53.0bn) the price requires 14.4-15.2%/yr FCF growth for ten years on the normalised FY26 base (1,884 - 715 = $1,169m), or 8.9-9.7%/yr on a smoothed 2-year-average base ($2.5bn - 715), versus the dossier's 6-8% base: implied_vs_base is above, not in_line. Post-cutoff (1 Oct 2026) FQ1 FY27 release guided FY27 revenue down high-single digits and adjusted EPS $1.15-1.35 (below the $1.58 'normalised' EPS used as the scenario start) with a $1.0bn Pace restructuring, which weakens the base case further.

NKE.scenario_basis: DV30 restated the dividend yield only: the original added ~1.6% (that is the $1.63 dividend per share in dollars); the yield is $1.64 / $35.75 = 4.6% (dividends declared $1.63 in FY2026). Same growth and multiple assumptions (start normalised EPS $1.58: bear flat EPS at 15x, base 7%/yr FCF growth at 20x, bull 12%/yr at 25x). The FY27 outlook issued 1 Oct 2026 (adjusted EPS $1.15-1.35) is below this start and is not reflected, so the base is optimistic.

LOW.thesis_one_line: America's #2 home-improvement retailer, priced for almost no growth, but its comp-sales streak is decelerating and recent growth is mostly acquisition-driven.
kill_criteria: Comparable sales turn negative (below 0.0%) for two consecutive quarters (trend has already gone +1.3% to +0.6% to +0.2%).
FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance is cut below the current $12.25 (already the low end of the original $12.25-12.75 range) at any subsequent quarterly release.
Estimated net debt/EBITDA (consolidated) rises above 3.5x (from an estimated ~2.7-2.8x currently).
Share repurchases remain at or near zero ($211M FY2025 run-rate) for four more consecutive quarters while GAAP stockholders' equity fails to improve from the 2026-07-31 level of -$7.4bn.
Free cash flow (OCF minus capex) for fiscal year 2026 comes in below fiscal 2025's approximately $7.65bn.
key_adverse_facts: Comparable sales growth has decelerated for three straight quarters (+1.3% to +0.6% to +0.2%), even as the company calls it a 'fifth consecutive quarter of positive comps.'
FY2026 guidance has been trimmed to the low end of every metric (sales, comps, margin, EPS) at the Q2 FY2026 release, six months after the year began, despite an 'affirm' in between.

Headline sales growth of +8-10% YoY in the last two quarters is substantially acquisition-driven (Foundation Building Materials, $8.8bn cash at a rich 13.4x EBITDA, closed 2025-10-09; Artisan Design Group), not organic.

Net debt rose to an estimated ~$34.4bn and stockholders' equity remains deeply negative (-$7.4bn to -$9.9bn across recent quarters) as buybacks were paused to help fund the FBM deal; free cash flow was flat YoY (~$7.65bn) despite +3.1% sales growth.
data_conflicts: The b1 quant snapshot's raw sales-growth-adjacent signals do not distinguish that recent headline revenue growth is acquisition-driven (FBM/ADG) rather than organic; the pct_bp (book/price) percentile of 0.09 looks like a quality problem but is mechanically an artefact of Lowe's structurally negative equity from historical buybacks, not distress.
LOW.confidence_in_thesis: medium-high: the valuation margin of safety (implied growth ~2.3%/yr vs. a 4-6%/yr base case) is large and the balance-sheet/M&A facts are confirmed from primary filings, but the comp-deceleration trend is real and should be watched closely at the next print.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for LOW (confirmed absent from v1_valuation_table.csv), so v1_verdict is null and there is nothing to reconcile against; the dossier's own reverse DCF implies only ~2.3%/yr 10-year FCF growth, clearly below even the bear case (0-1%/yr) let alone the 4-6%/yr base case, so the view is cheap.

LOW.scenario_basis: Starting FY2026 guided adjusted EPS ~$12.25 (low end of range); bear assumes comparable sales turn negative and the multiple holds near today's ~15.5x; base assumes 4-6%/yr FCF growth (continued Pro/online/home-services mix shift, gradual buyback resumption) at a stable ~15.5x multiple; bull assumes a housing-turnover recovery driving 8-10%/yr FCF growth and re-rating toward 18-19x; a ~2% dividend yield is added in each case.

MKC.thesis_one_line: High-quality spice and flavor leader, but the stock is really a bet on a pending, dilutive $45bn Unilever Foods merger needing antitrust and shareholder approval.
kill_criteria: The U.K. CMA's Phase 1 decision (due 2026-11-11) refers the deal to a Phase 2 in-depth investigation, or the U.S./E.U. authorities impose material forced divestitures beyond the already-announced Colman's mustard sale.
McCormick's shareholder vote on the transaction (once scheduled) fails, or is postponed beyond calendar 2027.
Organic sales growth (ex-acquisitions/FX, as reported each quarter) falls below 1% for two consecutive quarters (vs. the 1-3% guided for FY2026 and +1.7% delivered in Q2 FY2026).
FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance ($3.05-3.13) is cut below $3.00 at any subsequent quarterly release.

Disclosed pro forma net debt/adjusted EBITDA for the combined company exceeds 4.5x, or MKC's own standalone net debt/adjusted EBITDA rises materially above its current low-single-digit level as bridge financing is arranged ahead of close.
key_adverse_facts: McCormick agreed (2026-03-31) to combine with the majority of Unilever's Foods business in a ~$44.8bn deal ($15.7bn cash + $29.1bn stock); Unilever's own shareholders will receive 55.1% of the combined company and Unilever itself retains 9.9%, implying legacy McCormick shareholders are diluted to roughly 35% ownership of the combined entity.

The $15.7bn cash portion of the deal dwarfs McCormick's current balance-sheet capacity (total debt currently ~$4.9bn); a major new debt raise is required before close, and pro forma combined leverage has not been disclosed in sources reviewed.

The deal faces multiple live regulatory gates: the U.K. CMA opened a Phase 1 antitrust investigation with a decision due 2026-11-11 (Unilever is already preemptively divesting the Colman's mustard brand to address U.K. concerns), plus separate, unresolved U.S. and E.U. reviews and a McCormick shareholder vote whose scheduling was not confirmed in sources reviewed.

Trailing GAAP TTM P/E of ~8.0x (cited in the triage as evidence of cheapness) is a mechanical artefact of a one-time ~$850-900M non-cash gain from remeasuring McCormick's previously-held equity stake in McCormick de Mexico to fair value upon obtaining control (2026-01-02); it is not a usable valuation signal.

Underlying organic sales growth is only 1.7% (Q2 FY2026, guided 1-3% for the full year); the +16.7% headline reported growth in the last two quarters is ~11-13 points de Mexico consolidation plus ~2.7 points FX.
data_conflicts: b1's exclude_pending_deal flag is False for MKC, but the pending $45bn Unilever Foods combination is exactly the kind of pending-deal risk the v4 program has excluded other names for (WBD, KVUE, TECH, AES, NSC, D per v4/STATE.md); flagged for the lead to consider re-flagging this name.

Q03 triage's flagged conflict (trailing P/E 8.0x vs. NTM P/E 14.7x with a headline -45% forward EPS growth figure) is now fully resolved: it is caused by the one-time McCormick de Mexico remeasurement gain inflating trailing GAAP EPS (see key_adverse_facts); adjusted EPS, not trailing GAAP EPS, is the reliable base.

DV28: Ernst & Young was dismissed as auditor on 2026-09-24 (8-K 0000063754-26-000322, Item 4.01) because EY will not be independent after the Unilever Foods closing; the dossier stated no auditor change.
MKC.confidence_in_thesis: low: the standalone business is executing to plan, but the investment outcome for a holder today is dominated by an unresolved, multi-jurisdiction regulatory process and a shareholder vote whose date and outcome could not be confirmed in sources reviewed.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for MKC, so nothing to reconcile. DV28 restatement: the dossier's 7.5% rate on an EV basis was replaced by an equity-basis reverse DCF (market cap $12.9bn, FCF after SBC $694m, cost of equity 7.9% = 5.17% + 4.14% x beta ~0.66, terminal 2.5%): implied ~2.2%/yr (3.6% at 8.5%), below the 4-5%/yr standalone base, so the standalone view is modestly cheap; the label is secondary to the pending-deal risk that drives WATCH.

MKC.scenario_basis: Starting FY2026 guided adjusted EPS midpoint $3.09; bear assumes the Unilever Foods deal is blocked, abandoned, or closes on worse-than-disclosed dilution/leverage terms, keeping the multiple depressed near 13-14x; base assumes the deal closes around mid-2027 near disclosed terms with standalone organic growth continuing at 1-3%/yr and a stable ~15.5x multiple; bull assumes successful integration and the claimed EPS accretion materialize, driving re-rating toward ~18x; a ~1.9% dividend yield is added throughout.
